results.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must report every #[cfg(unix)] item that has no #[cfg(windows)], #[cfg(not(unix))] or portable counterpart, unless an approved exception declaration opts it out.
results.quote:
atm-core can remove its PORT-010 exclusions and get zero false alarms, while real Windows gaps are still reported.
Definition question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "real Windows gap = a cfg(unix) item with no Windows, cfg(not(unix)) or portable counterpart" Rand: "yes"
Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "ANC-015 against ANC-017. ANC-015 says to report any `cfg(unix)` item with no portable counterpart. ANC-017 says to exempt public POSIX-only helpers that have no Windows counterpart. They overlap" Rand (2026-10-30): "we must have an approved exception path to knowingly opt out."
results.context: Phase M planning; Rand approved the sentence, answered 'yes' to the definition question and ruled on the ANC-015/ANC-017 conflict, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-30
results.deterministic_check: A port010 fixture with a cfg(unix) fn and no Windows, cfg(not(unix)) or portable counterpart reports PORT-010 when no approved exception declaration names it.
